observations.result: The frozen selection verifier rejected live stats/registry hash drift and cumulative-download changes. The output did not report a ranking or repository mismatch, so the frozen top-25 ordering was retained rather than silently refreshed.

The official stats snapshot returned HTTP 200 with 2225364 bytes and SHA-256 9f397fd41c4ec66074c9d63732191dc34db1c28437c9bedfa76e5687c1754d97; the registry snapshot returned HTTP 200 with 2218664 bytes and SHA-256 973e2b116d930d7615a45d1fb9d9f05d49a1ed4b1dc3f3223da8c516bfe633d9.

Seven recorded references passed; electron-security remained HTTP 200 with 170321 bytes but its SHA-256 changed from 282670ba3be0773a4ef933ad9bd42feaf33e4be83916f7e405b7ba2da2bc5a9f to 9221c933ae48e72a2e153fd8eb74bc0b4c70e8880a81b9d1ab15f046eb2330e8.
The Electron security URL returned HTTP 200, content type text/html, 170321 bytes and SHA-256 9221c933ae48e72a2e153fd8eb74bc0b4c70e8880a81b9d1ab15f046eb2330e8.

A live 27-artifact network verification was interrupted after more than five minutes of bounded fetch retries; no manifest or release pin was changed. The earlier successful pinned-asset verification remains in 2026-09-10-p0.2-selection-drift.json.

disposition: Keep the frozen plugin-selection snapshot, stable Obsidian 1.13.7 baseline and immutable release-asset pins until a deliberate reviewed refresh records the new retrieval time and consequences. Treat the mutable Electron documentation hash drift as a provenance follow-up, not as permission to weaken the reference gate.
